spec.title: Recovery after interrupted reasoning and execution

scope.title: 1. Facts survive; unfinished confidence does not

p.RECOVERY-SCOPE: This is a coordination protocol for provider overload, rate limits, exhausted quota, timeout, crash, compaction, and a change of chat, model or account. It does not implement a provider client, retry daemon, account switcher or scheduler. The driver applies it using the harness and ordinary inspectable artifacts. Every recovery remains within current owner authority, including planning-only instructions, execution holds and explicit stops.

p.REASONING-LOSS: Private unfinished reasoning may be irretrievably lost. Do not claim to restore it from a summary. Recover durable facts, artifacts, accepted decisions and evidence; reconstruct the next decision afresh from those inputs. An unrecorded conclusion is not an accepted decision. A surviving narrative is a claim to check, not proof.

p.STATE-COMPATIBILITY: Keep the existing schema-1 plan, stable ids, dependencies, mandate dispositions and acceptance tiers. No recovery status, second queue, mandatory session record, custody claim or handoff is introduced. Ordinary notes, task reports, tool/job receipts and existing node evidence can carry recovery facts. A compact working packet is a view over those sources, never another authoritative plan.

td.TRANSIENT-SIGNAL: A provider explicitly reports temporary overload, transient unavailability or a rate limit with a retry/reset hint.

td.TRANSIENT-RESPONSE: Use the bounded retry episode below when the request is safe to repeat. A status code alone may be ambiguous: quota exhaustion can also be reported as a rate limit. Use the provider's non-secret error classification and hints.

td.CAPACITY-SIGNAL: The provider reports exhausted account quota, insufficient entitlement or a limit that needs an external reset.

td.CAPACITY-RESPONSE: Do not repeatedly probe unchanged capacity. Preserve work and use the known reset time as an external condition; if unknown, say it is unknown. Continue useful authorized work that does not need the unavailable resource, or stop with that blocker. Quota exhaustion is neither a product failure nor acceptance.

td.REQUEST-SIGNAL: Authentication, permission, invalid request, unsupported capability or a prompt/context too large.

td.REQUEST-RESPONSE: Do not retry the unchanged request as though it were overload. Resolve the actual input, configuration or authority problem. For context size, rebuild a bounded packet from the complete durable plan without dropping obligations. Never copy credentials into reports or silently switch accounts.

td.PRODUCT-SIGNAL: A reproducible check/assertion fails on the intended subject, or a required behavior is observably wrong.

td.PRODUCT-RESPONSE: Use normal diagnosis, repair and review. Every repeated attempt needs a changed input, circumstance, hypothesis or method that explains why it may add evidence; provider backoff is not a repair strategy.

td.UNKNOWN-SIGNAL: A connection breaks or output disappears after a tool/job may have started or finished.

td.UNKNOWN-RESPONSE: The outcome is unknown. Reconcile the actual operation and surviving artifacts before deciding to retry. A missing final message is not a failed operation.

p.CAPTURE-FAILURE: Capture only the necessary non-secret facts: affected existing node and operation, input subject, observed error class/time, request or job id when available, retry hint, surviving artifact locations, attempts already consumed and next discriminating check. Record uncertainty explicitly. Never preserve raw sensitive provider bodies, authorization headers, tokens or environment dumps for convenience.

p.RETRY-IDENTITY: An episode belongs to one logical operation and input subject under the observed failure condition, not to one chat or account. Rewording the prompt, changing a worker, account or model, or reopening a session does not erase consumed attempts. A shared outage does not justify launching many equivalent requests in parallel. Use the existing report, packet, job journal or node evidence to retain the episode; there is no prescribed new file format.

p.RETRY-BUDGET: Honor a project/runtime retry policy within owner authority and record the effective limits before automatic retry. If none exists, the default is at most three total submissions including the initial request, within ten minutes from the episode's first failure. These limits bound resource retries, not campaign size or overall implementation effort. Count known SDK/harness retries within the same budget; do not stack independent retry loops. When hidden retries prevent a trustworthy remaining budget, inspect runtime status or stop automatic retries and report that uncertainty. If a restart loses the budget evidence, do not assume zero attempts or grant a fresh default budget.

p.RETRY-DELAY: For an eligible transient failure, the default delays before the two possible retries are five and ten seconds, each with zero to twenty-five percent positive jitter. A valid server retry/reset hint is a minimum delay and takes precedence when longer. Do not retry before it, truncate it to fit the budget, or retry after the episode's deadline. A hint beyond the remaining window makes the resource temporarily unavailable. Respect stricter harness waiting limits; split a permitted wait into responsive intervals or stop with the next eligible time. Never busy-loop or simulate elapsed time.

p.RETRY-EXIT: Stop retries on success, owner stop, exhausted attempt/time budget, a permanent error, ambiguous effect, or evidence that the operation is already live. A paused episode stays paused across restart. A new automatic episode requires an observed material change that resolves the previous condition, such as a confirmed quota reset, restored service or observed available capacity through an owner-configured provider, or explicit owner renewal. Record that reason and retain the old episode evidence. Elapsed chat time, a new account label, a new prompt name or a desire to keep trying is not renewal evidence. A read-only status check must itself be bounded; do not disguise indefinite retrying as status polling.

p.ACCOUNT-CHANGE: The owner may change account or model using the client. The coordinator does not automate credential switching, move secrets, or treat another identity as an escape from provider restrictions. Verify the newly available capability through normal authorized client state and retain the logical episode's spent budget; renewal requires the changed availability or explicit authority described in `RETRY-EXIT`. On the same operating-system user and exact repository/worktree binding, this is ordinary continuation with the existing plan, not a formal handoff. Different bindings follow the normal context-resolution rules.

p.WAITING-CLAIMS: Report a known next eligible time, remaining retry budget and practical next action when useful. Do not promise to wake, resume or notify later unless an external scheduler has actually been authorized and configured. The package itself creates no timer or automation. A pause for unavailable capacity never marks the campaign complete.

p.REQUEST-VERSUS-EFFECT: Repeating a model generation request and repeating its tool actions are different decisions. A fresh generation should receive the verified current state and remaining task; it must not blindly replay an earlier transcript. Even a generation or tool request can create a billable job or external effect. Where completion is ambiguous, inspect request/job status before resubmission.

p.RECONCILE-EFFECT: Use an available job id, operation receipt, process status, remote object/version, transaction state or durable postcondition to determine whether the operation is live, succeeded, failed without effect, or partly applied. Reuse the original idempotency key only when the operation contract supports it; never generate a new key to retry the same ambiguous effect. If postconditions prove success, record and review it without replay. If live, observe that job within the bounded runtime policy. If partial, repair or roll back only within existing authority. If the outcome cannot be established and duplicate effects matter, stop that operation with the unresolved fact; continue independent safe work.

p.RETAIN-WORK: Inventory diffs, files, reports, test output, logs and active worker jobs before regenerating anything. Keep usable partial output even if the producer's final turn failed. Do not launch a replacement writer until the old writer is known stopped or isolated from the new write perimeter. Distinguish a live worker from an observed conflicting central writer; ordinary stale metadata proves neither.

p.RETRY-NOT-ACCEPTANCE: Successful retry recovers execution, not acceptance. Worker claims and recovered partial work remain candidates until the central review and required gates establish their declared tier. Durable accepted evidence remains valid for its unchanged subject. A missing log needed to establish a new claim calls for targeted reproduction; it does not erase unrelated accepted history.

p.CHECKPOINT-ECONOMY: At a useful decision, review or artifact boundary, persist the small set of facts a fresh coordinator would otherwise have to rediscover. Before an operation with consequential external effects, retain its purpose, input subject and recovery/idempotency identity when available so an interrupted acknowledgement can be reconciled. Use ordinary existing artifacts and evidence surfaces; do not create a universal checkpoint ritual or serialize each thought. A record is useful only if its discovery path is available from the current task or existing node evidence.

p.CHECKPOINT-CONTENTS: A bounded continuity note may contain existing node ids, verified input identities, accepted boundary, candidate locations, live jobs, attempts consumed, concise decision conclusions and their reasons, unresolved alternatives, the next discriminating check and literal continuation command if known. Separate observed facts, hypotheses and owner rulings. Persist enough rationale to reassess a decision; neither demand nor claim preservation of hidden chain-of-thought.

facts.RESUME-ORIENT: Resolve current owner scope and exact context; read settings and the complete plan; inspect actual repository/input state. Preserve execution holds. A new model/account does not inherit authority from a confident summary.
facts.RESUME-RECONCILE: Reconcile live jobs, ambiguous effects and surviving candidates. Recover consumed retry and mutation budgets from evidence. Do not start another writer or issue another effect while its predecessor's status is materially unknown.
facts.RESUME-REASON: Read concise decision notes where present; check them against governing sources and actual state. Reconstruct unrecorded reasoning as new tentative work. If there was no checkpoint, use the tree, plan and inspectable artifacts; their absence creates uncertainty to resolve, not a compulsory handoff or restart from zero.
facts.RESUME-VERIFY: Compare evidence subjects to current relevant inputs. Retain unchanged accepted evidence; rerun only affected or unverifiable steps and the unrun tail of an owed gate. Preserve the complete required step/case denominator, including compatible earlier results, and report aggregate proof honestly. A new HEAD or model alone does not require starting the full panel again. Apply @spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/flows/multi-user-planning/verification-selection#PANEL-RESUMPTION. A recovered candidate still receives central review.
facts.RESUME-CONTINUE: Update existing node evidence and state only as justified, refresh the derived goal if stale, and select the next bounded authorized action. Status/planning-only requests finish within that scope; an execution instruction permits continuation without a new permission ceremony.

scenarios.title: 6. Acceptance examples for drivers and reviewers

facts.CASE-OVERLOAD: **Temporary overload:** a pure request fails and names a twenty-second retry delay. One retry waits at least twenty seconds, consumes the second submission and succeeds. No source test fails by implication; no second retry runs after success.
facts.CASE-LONG-HINT: **Unavailable capacity:** a retry hint is thirty minutes away under the default ten-minute window. Preserve the task and report the eligible time. Do not poll every few seconds, sleep past the budget, promise an unconfigured wakeup or mark the campaign complete.
facts.CASE-ACCOUNT-RESUME: **Quota mid-decision:** an account exhausts quota after a diff was written and before a verdict. The owner opens the same checkout with another account. Read the complete plan, recover the candidate diff and spent episode budget, reconstruct the missing decision and run affected checks. Keep accepted nodes and execution holds; neither accept the diff nor repeat its edits from a summary alone.
facts.CASE-PUBLISH-ACK: **Lost publication acknowledgement:** a publication request times out. Read remote state or the original operation receipt before retrying. Matching published content is evidence to review; a new publication with a new idempotency key is not the recovery default.
facts.CASE-LIVE-WORKER: **Coordinator disappears:** a worker is still running when a fresh coordinator arrives. Observe its job, retain its partial files and wait within policy or explicitly stop/isolate it before replacement. Do not create two writers merely because the old chat is gone.
facts.CASE-MUTATION-RESUME: **Interrupted diagnostic:** one mutation has already produced a green result when context is lost. Restore the original bytes, adjudicate equivalence, reachability and the contract using the existing observation, and use the named alternative if needed. A new account does not earn another mutant.
facts.CASE-NO-CHECKPOINT: **Crash without notes:** tree state contains a partial change with no durable decision. Inventory it as candidate, reconstruct the intended obligation from existing node ids and sources, and choose a bounded next check. The absence of hidden reasoning is neither evidence of correctness nor a reason to discard useful work.
facts.CASE-PANEL-RESUME: **Fail-fast panel:** three required steps passed, the fourth failed, and two never ran. A fix invalidates the fourth and one earlier step. Rerun those two and the unrun tail, reusing the other passing results only after checking their full relevant input closures. Preserve all six obligations and required cases; report aggregate coverage, not a fictional successful full invocation. If earlier validity is unknown, rerun those steps too.
